item.title: EU pledges Kyiv aid despite Orbán threats on war anniversary
item.description: Hungary's pro-Russian veto is being seen by diplomats as a temporary glitch, while other states passed a law anyway to loan money to Ukraine.

item.title: The shocking return of anti-personnel mines to Europe
item.description: At the start of last year, all 27 EU member states were signed up to the Ottawa Convention, banning the use, production, stockpiling and transfer of anti-personnel mines. Now Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Finalnd have withdrawn — with silence from Brussels.

item.title: Merz urges more German-Chinese ‘cooperation’ as Beijing visit begins
item.description: Despite soaring trade imbalances and EU pressure, German chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed the need to fortify diplomatic and economic relations with China on his first Beijing visit.

item.title: Listen: How Poland is preparing for a potential war?
item.description: Poland isn’t just preparing for war — it’s rewriting the rulebook on how to get ready. Meanwhile, the rest of the EU is slowly catching up on defence. What can we learn from Poland’s approach?

item.title: Brussels calls it ‘simplification’ – it’s actually a rollback of workers rights
item.description: Brussels’ drive to cut digital “burdens” is spilling into labour law. A recent paper by lobby group BusinessEurope calls for a sweeping “labour market omnibus” to reduce obligations under EU social law, raising fears that competitiveness rhetoric could undermine workers’ rights and weaken Europe’s social model.

item.title: NGOs want ex-Meta MEP removed from EU digital rules relaxation
item.description: The open letter on Wednesday from NGOs Corporate Europe Observatory, Transparency International and five other organisations argues Finnish centre-right MEP Aura Salla’s ties to Meta constitute an irreconcilable conflict of interest in the digital file.

item.title: Hungary and Slovakia in standoff with Ukraine over broken Russian oil pipe
item.description: Russian oil via the Druzhba pipeline has halted, sparking tensions between Slovakia, Hungary and Ukraine, although Brussels says supplies remain stable. In contrast, Kyiv builds cyber ties with other EU countries while Baltic states bolster border defences.

item.title: MEPs rally behind ex-commissioner Breton after US sanctions
item.description: Thierry Breton spoke to the European Parliament on Wednesday, where MEPs expressed their solidarity and reaffirmed their support for the EU’s Digital rulebook.

item.title: MEPs ask where EU billions for Africa came from
item.description: The EU commission must reveal how billions of euros in funds for its Global Gateway projects have been raised, say MEPs

item.title: Anti-LGBTI tactics now a blueprint to crush dissent, says report
item.description: A new report suggests Europe has entered a new phase, whereby critical voices are increasingly silenced by authoritarian-leaning governments spanning Hungary to Russia and Turkey.
